description.narrative: The project's overall objective is to enhance public integrity and accountability by promoting civic activism in combating corruption. By pursuing this impact goal, KDI-TI Kosova aims for state institutions to undertake actions that enhance integrity by implementing and, if needed, improving anticorruption standards and practices influenced by civic activism. KDI-TI Kosova has designed three specific objectives (outcomes) which collectively will contribute to the improvements in the fight against corruption: Outcome 1 - To increase the engagement of young generations of community-based leaders in the prevention of corruption. Outcome 2 - To enhance public integrity values, practices and standards by using evidencebased data by citizens, victims and witnesses of corruption. Outcome 3 - To strengthen prevention and determent of corruption through increased civil society, media and state institutions cooperation and collective endeavors of the program. The proposed project is concentrated in the empowerment and interaction of five key target groups (youth, witnesses and victims of corruption, civil society organizations, media, and state institutions), which is instrumental for creating platforms to push for public integrity to improve institutional accountability and ownership. This approach will support the creation of a critical mass which will be able to influence public discourse and drive action against political corruption.

Projektets övergripande mål är att öka den offentliga integriteten och ansvarsskyldigheten genom att främja medborgaraktivism i kampen mot korruption. Genom en ökad medborgaraktivism lyfts problemen till statliga institutioner för att vidta åtgärder och, om nödvändigt, förbättra antikorruptionsstandarder och praxis.
Projektets målgrupper är ungdomar, vittnen och offer av korruption, civilsamhällesorganisationer, media, statliga institutioner och offentliga myndigheter.

The project's overall objective is to enhance public integrity and accountability by promoting civic activism in combating corruption. In pursuing this impact goal, KDI-Transparency International Kosova aims for state institutions to undertake actions that enhance integrity by implementing and, if needed, improving anti-corruption standards and practices influenced by civic activism. KDI has designed three specific objectives (outcomes) which collectively will contribute to the improvements in the fight against corruption by facilitating a climate in which youth, witnesses and victims of corruption, state institutions, civil society organizations, and media, are willing to openly discuss, learn, cooperate and work towards solutions influencing improved public integrity.

description.narrative:
During 2025 KDI organized a total of 19 training sessions across eight regions of Kosova. Instead of online trainings, which proved ineffective in 2024, KDI shifted to delivering sessions directly in high schools and universities, thereby increasing both outreach and accessibility. In total, 551 young participants took part in these trainings, representing diverse regions, ethnic backgrounds, and social groups. Participation showed a predominance of female participants, contributing to strengthening the role of young women in discussions on integrity and public accountability.
Out of 400 young people who completed the training during 2024 KDI selected approximately 50 participants for the two-day Anti-Corruption Camp (Super Academy). Through targeted modules and practical exercises, participants developed a more strategic understanding of how to engage in public processes and contribute to addressing corruption-related issues in their communities. Following the completion of the training cycle and the development of initial advocacy ideas, some participants went on to design and implement concrete initiatives focusing on political finance transparency, environmental governance, and responsible public communication.
At the beginning of 2025, KDI conducted a structured review and update of its training modules from the feedback collected during the 2024 training cycle. The revision focused on strengthening the practical relevance of the content and aligning it more closely with participants needs and experiences.
Throughout the reporting period, Advocacy and Legal Advice Center (ALAC) received and handled a total of 64 cases, covering a wide range of issues. These included labour rights violations, concerns related to the work of the prosecutorial and judicial systems, cases in the health and education sectors, abuse of office, local governance issues, and whistleblower-related matters. The increased number of cases reported by employees within public institutions indicates growing trust in KDIs reporting mechanisms, as well as in the confidentiality and reliability of the legal support provided through ALAC.
During 2025, KDI published two policy briefs addressing key governance and electoral challenges in Kosovo:
'Parliamentary Blockages and the Undermining of Institutional Integrity' examined the impact of legislative deadlock on institutional functioning and accountability. The brief analyzed procedural and political obstacles affecting the Assembly and proposed concrete measures to strengthen institutional integrity and prevent similar blockages in the future.
'Women in the 2025 Local Elections: Between Quotas and Electoral Reality' assessed the participation of women in local elections, focusing on the gap between legal guarantees and actual representation. The brief provided recommendations aimed at improving the effectiveness of gender quotas and strengthening inclusiveness within electoral processes.
KDIs advocacy actions contributed to increased public understanding of the institutional crisis and strengthening civic pressure for accountability. The #ShtetiNëPauzë platform enabled coordinated civil society engagement at a national level, while the combination of public communication, research, and symbolic actions ensured sustained visibility of the issue.
KDI positioned itself as a consistent and credible source of legal, procedural, and governance-related interpretation. Through more than 15 press statements, the organization addressed each critical phase of the institutional crisis, including the constitution of the Assembly, verification of mandates, respect for constitutional deadlines, and the conduct of political actors
During 2024, KDI initiated the Thematic Anti-Corruption Forum, an informal mechanism designed to enhance cooperation between civil society, media, and public institutions in the fight against corruption. During 2025, the context for implementing this activity changed significantly. The Agency for Prevention of Corruption took the initiative to formalize and institutionalize the Anti-Corruption Forum in cooperation with KDI, shifting the focus toward establishing a structured and sustainable platform for cooperation among civil society, media, and public institutions.
During 2025, KDI implemented a sub-granting scheme aimed at strengthening civil society engagement in combating corruption and promoting political integrity. Through this mechanism, KDI supported initiatives focused on political financing transparency, integrity in decision-making, and accountability in the use of public resources. The call generated strong interest, with a total of 59 applications submitted, of which five sub-grants were awarded to the highest-ranked local organizations.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
